This update brings together 2.0.10.0 and 2.0.11.0 from the beta channel.

If you use the Live TV allow-list behind a reverse proxy: add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings. Without that, every request through the proxy counts as coming from the proxy, and if its address is on your list, everyone gets in. The help text now says so.

Fixed: with Live TV set up on two or more providers, the guide never used your providers' XMLTV files. They were combined into one file that could not be read past the first provider, so the guide always fell back to the simpler per-channel listings and lost categories, ratings and the other details XMLTV carries. Each provider's file is now read on its own. If one provider's file is missing or broken, only that provider's channels fall back, and the others keep their full guide (found and fixed by dillardblom).

Fixed: when two providers used the same guide id for different channels, one of them got no guide, or showed the other provider's programmes. Guide ids are now matched per provider (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: when your provider's XMLTV guide came through cut off part way, building the guide never finished. Each request for the EPG URL kept one CPU core busy until Jellyfin gave up, and the guide stayed empty. A broken file now falls back to fetching the guide per channel, as it already did when the file was missing, and no programme is listed twice (by dillardblom).

Fixed: with Dispatcharr mode on, every sync worker logged in to Dispatcharr at the same time when a sync started. Dispatcharr's login limit refused most of them, and those workers fell back to the Xtream API for the first minutes. There is now one login shared by all of them, and it waits its turn like every other request (reported by dillardblom).

This update brings together 2.0.2.0 to 2.0.9.0 from the beta channel.

If you use Live TV with the Native Tuner only, open the Live TV tab after updating and turn off the new "Publish Playlists" switch. It stays on for anyone who already had Live TV enabled, so an M3U tuner or TiviMate setup keeps working, but the native tuner does not need it.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: a single unreadable value from your provider, such as an empty value where a number belongs, no longer makes content disappear. versions.changelog:
## 兼容性说明

为了避免升级 Jellyfin 12 后可能与 Jellyfin 10.11 不兼容的情况，保留此版本作为 Jellyfin 10.11 的最后一个版本。

后续插件将不再考虑 Jellyfin 10.11 的兼容性，若出现不兼容情况，可以下载此版本。

## 新功能与改进

- 增加按用户管理 Bangumi 授权，以及 NSFW 播放记录的私密上报选项。
- 增加缺失 Bangumi ID 的补全工具和 `bangumi.ini` 媒体库管理功能，改进批量选择及刷新反馈。
- 增加动画搜索偏好和优先使用原始标题搜索的配置，支持自定义 Bangumi 网站地址。
- 引入 Anitomy 剧集解析器，改进文件名、集数和多季度识别。
- 增强音乐元数据与播放记录同步，调整插件设置页面。

## 问题修复

- 修复 Bangumi 图片地址和搜索结果处理问题。
- 修复剧集与季度未读取 `bangumi.ini`、未知季度和重复剧集扫描中的特别篇识别问题。
- 修复音乐刮削中的元数据丢失及艺人类型筛选问题。
- 修复 infobox 解析死循环及重复字段处理。
- 改进异步请求、取消操作、评分刷新和播放状态缓存处理。

**完整更新记录**：https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/compare/1.7.6...1.7.7

## New Features 增加了重复剧集检测小工具，用于替换字幕组、发布 V2 版时自动清理旧版本 ## What's Changed * fix: handle null and empty ChineseName correctly by @chu-shen in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/232 * fix: Emby plugin support for macOS ARM and .NET 6 runtime by @nihs903222 in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/233 * fix: implement IHasSupportedExternalIdentifiers for Emby by @sjtuross in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/236 * 修复Subject的PersonInfos或Characters拉取失败导致整个Subject的元数据拉取失败的问题 by @HydrogensaysHDT in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/238 ## New Contributors * @nihs903222 made their first contribution in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/233 * @sjtuross made their first contribution in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/236 * @HydrogensaysHDT made their first contribution in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/238 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/compare/1.7.5...1.7.6

## What's Changed
* 支持人物搜索
* 为 Emby 添加 bangumi.ini 支持 by @luoboQAQ in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/224
* 优化 markdown 换行转换，对于不支持 markdown 显示的第三方播放器更友好
* 修复元数据中 `Bangumi ID` 显示为 `Bangumi 专辑 ID` 的问题

name: Marquee Companion [✓✓]
description:
Adds server-side library filtering by media-stream characteristics that Jellyfin's core API can't express (video dynamic range, codecs, audio channel count, and spatial audio), opt-in recovery of missing release dates from file names or date added, authenticated Apple Watch media grants, and server-stored profile PINs. The filtering API exposes a paginated, BaseItemDto-compatible endpoint and a capability endpoint for client feature-detection. Release-date recovery is selected per library and can preview changes before applying them.

versions.changelog:
- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.

  and bundled mail dependencies. Existing email mappings and Jellyfin accounts are untouched.

  from Dashboard > Scheduled Tasks.

- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.
- Adds the seamless Marquee Companion panel to Jellyfin Web without manual web-client changes. - Adds paired Jellyfin 10/.NET 9 and Jellyfin 12/.NET 10 package builds.

## v1.7.2.0
### Fixes
- When LRCLIB rate limits a request, the plugin now waits as long as LRCLIB asks before moving on to the next song. It also backs off on 503 errors now. Thanks to @tranxuanthang -> #61
- Songs that got rate limited are no longer marked as "no lyrics found". Before, they were skipped for days.
- The lyrics task stops early when LRCLIB keeps rate limiting it. The next run continues where it stopped. -> #60

## v1.7.1.0
### New
- Redesigned settings page.
- New "Remove plain lyrics that hide synced lyrics" option, on by default. Turn it off if other apps use the lyrics files in your music folder.
### Fixes
- Synced lyrics now show up even when a plain .txt sits next to the song. Before, Jellyfin kept showing the plain lyrics and the task re-downloaded the synced ones every run. -> #59

## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

For Jellyfin 12. Fixes for the three open issues.

- Newer OpenAI models work now. They refuse `max_tokens` and only accept the default temperature, so the plugin switches to `max_completion_tokens` and drops the temperature on its own, then remembers it for that model. You can also pick the field in the settings ("Reply length limit field"). Fixes #4.
- You can exclude libraries from AI Search. Ticked libraries are left out of the index, the AI search popup and the AI matches in Jellyfin's search, but still show up in Jellyfin's normal title search. Fixes #3.
- Building the index with a model that gives no embeddings (a reranker, or llama.cpp with `--pooling rank`) now stops with a clear message saying so, instead of a JSON error. If only a few titles fail, the build skips them and tells you how many. Fixes #2.

For Jellyfin 12. Searching is much faster, and you can now see where each result comes from.

What's new:
- Jellyfin's own search no longer waits for AI Search. Title results show up right away.
- AI matches get their own "AI Search" row under Jellyfin's results, with a short reason under each title.
- If a chat model is set up, it writes a one-line reason for each AI match a few seconds later.
- The plugin speaks French or English. By default it follows each user's Jellyfin language, or you can pick one in the settings.
- The search model is loaded as soon as you open the search page, so the first search isn't slow anymore.
- Repeated searches are almost instant, and the AI popup no longer loads your whole library before searching.

Fixes:
- The search page no longer jumps up or down while results and reasons load.
- Opening the AI search button no longer scrolls the page back to the top.
- The search history list in the popup is back to its normal layout.
- Remote search works again for searches made with an API key.
- Search log files no longer start with a byte-order mark.

TV and mobile apps still get AI matches mixed into Jellyfin's results, waiting at most 2 seconds for them. Jellyfin 10.11 servers stay on 1.1.1.0.

For Jellyfin 12. Jellyfin's own search now also finds titles by meaning, shown in the usual Movies, Shows and Episodes rows after the title matches. New options: turn it on or off, only use it for searches that look like a sentence, limit how many matches it adds, hide the AI search button completely (native search only), and keep a log of every search for a few days so an admin or API key can collect them.

description:
Adds secure, expiring guest-share links for Jellyfin items using temporary hidden users, one-use token redemption, restrictive policies, and scheduled cleanup.

versions.changelog: Fixes shared movies failing with "media could not be found" when an intro plugin like Local Intros is installed (#23). The intros aren't part of the share, so the guest couldn't open them and playback stopped before the movie. Guests now skip intros, and any video or audio a guest can't open is left out of what the server sends them, whichever plugin or endpoint it came from.
Fixes share links on Jellyfin 12 and the ShareLink button missing on new Docker installs.

Fixes redemption on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and later (#19). Jellyfin changed the signature of the method the plugin uses to set a guest's password, so every link failed with a MissingMethodException and the guest landed on the dead-link page. The plugin now picks whichever version of that method the server has, so the same build works on every 10.11 release. Tested on 10.11.8 and 10.11.11.

Guests are now blocked from other plugins' API endpoints on the server, not just hidden from their UI in the browser. A share guest holds a real Jellyfin token, so anything that only hid a button left the endpoint answering it. Jellyfin's own API is untouched: the share tag already limits it to the shared title, and playback needs it. The config page lists your installed plugins with a checkbox each, so you can let one through when it genuinely needs to serve guests, such as an intro skipper. The guest hidden selectors setting is renamed to say what it is: cosmetic, it tidies the view and enforces nothing. Also fixes the dashboard devices page coming up empty after a share expired: deleting a guest left its device row behind, and a device whose user is missing makes Jellyfin fail the whole device listing rather than skip one row.

Fixes a season share exposing the rest of the series: the tag was going onto the season's parent series, and Jellyfin treats a parent's tags as belonging to all of its children, so every other season became visible to the guest. Tagging now only ever goes downwards. Take this update if you have shared a season with a link that is still live. Also in this release: a link can be made multi-use from the create popup so several people can use it until it expires, with a configurable ceiling on how many watch at once (ten by default), and the dashboard gains a "Clean up finished links" button that removes revoked, expired and failed records.

The ShareLink button now sits in its own section at the bottom of the item menu, and only appears for a movie, series, season or episode instead of turning up on things like a cast member. It is properly admin only again: the current user was cached for the whole page, so switching accounts in the same tab could leave the button visible to a normal user (the server always refused them). Share tags are hidden from everyone except admins, on the title and in the tag filter. Security: one-use links can no longer be redeemed twice, the configured maximum expiry is respected, the raw token is dropped from storage when a link dies, the token secret file is 0600, guest accounts can no longer sign in from the login page at all, and the runtime reflection shims around Jellyfin's APIs are gone.

Series and seasons can now be shared, not just single movies and episodes: the share tags the whole tree so the guest can browse and play everything inside it, and cleanup strips it all again. Expired or invalid links now show a friendly page that redirects to the Jellyfin home instead of raw JSON. The guest hidden selectors setting now defaults to empty.

ShareLink button on the item menu, temporary guest users confined by tag policy, expiring links with a date/time picker, admin dashboard with revoke, and a configurable guest lockdown that hides tag/genre/studio/cast links, the add-to-playlist and add-to-collection actions, and other plugins' UI. The creation popup is localized in English and French. Guest sessions are now minted server side: no password is ever stored or sent anywhere, the guest page only carries a session token, and expired guests are cleaned up every 30 minutes.

- **Metadata Refresh Detection**: Implemented HasChanged check using file timestamps so library refreshes detect updated assets on disk.

Official Release 3.3.5

- **Direct Image Application**: Streams and persists image updates directly using internal provider APIs upon receiving events.
- **Enhanced Configuration Page**: Added Real-Time Sync toggle, Posterizarr URL input, and API key configuration with live connection test diagnostics.
- **Volume Latency Tolerance**: Added 2-second retry loop for newly created image files.

Official Release 3.3.3

- **Persistent State Caching**: Added `posterizarr_sync_cache.json` in the plugin data directory to track file sizes, timestamps, and image metadata. Unchanged assets are skipped instantly in memory with zero network I/O.
- **Directory & File Caching**: Added `AssetPathResolver` to cache root library shares and folder file listings. Reduces tens of thousands of remote SMB/NFS round-trips to a single query per media folder.
- **Parallel Async Sync Task**: Upgraded `PosterizarrSyncTask` to use `Parallel.ForEachAsync` with adaptive concurrency, replacing single-threaded sequential processing.
- **Tiered Image Verification**: Added 4KB header and file-length pre-checks to eliminate continuous ~30 MB/s full-file MD5 hash calculations across the network.
- **Debug Mode Toggle**: Debug messages (`[Posterizarr DEBUG]`) are now directly controlled by the plugin's `EnableDebugMode` setting and visible in the Jellyfin log viewer without changing server logging configurations.
- **Emby Optimization**: Added same-path timestamp comparison to prevent double-hashing identical local files in Emby.
- **Performance Benchmark**: Successfully verified on a 39,000-item library, reducing task runtime from **32m 51s to 13 seconds (~151x faster)** with near-zero network and disk utilization.

Official Release 3.3.2

- **Jellyfin 12.0.x & 10.11.x Multi-Targeting**: Compiled for both `.NET 9` (Jellyfin 10.11.x) and `.NET 10` (Jellyfin 12.0.x) with target-specific ABI dependencies (`10.11.0.0` and `12.0.0.0`).
- **Automated Dual Packaging**: Manifest and release pipelines now generate separate distribution archives (`Posterizarr.Plugin_v3.3.2.zip` and `Posterizarr.Plugin_v3.3.2-jf12.zip`).

versions.changelog: When Jellyfin played a video without converting it, the trickplay playlist could name the wrong video format (for example HEVC for a 10-bit H.264 file), so the Apple TV prepared the wrong decoder and took much longer to start. The playlist now names the format Jellyfin actually sends, including 10-bit H.264 (High 10). No change for HDR or Dolby Vision videos.

Videos whose HEVC stream declares a level above 5.0 (common with certain x265 encodes) were rejected by the Apple TV when served through the trickplay-enabled playlist, and the player fell back to the thumbnail track. The playlist now also offers a level 5.0 entry, the same approach Jellyfin uses for its own playlists, so these videos play normally with scrubbing thumbnails intact. No change for other videos.

- Fixed: trickplay playlists and image segments now enforce each user's library access and parental controls. Previously, any signed-in user could request the scrubbing thumbnails of items outside their allowed libraries.
- Improved: the dashboard's item list loads dramatically faster on large libraries (it no longer reads every cached playlist from disk just to show cache status).
- Improved: changing "Concurrent encodes" now takes effect immediately — no server restart needed.
- Fixed: corrupt video files could make HDR detection time out, producing washed-out thumbnails for HDR content.
- Fixed: searching with an extremely large season or episode number could error the item list.
- Hardened the release pipeline: build steps are now pinned to exact, immutable versions.

After updating, restart your server once as usual. No cache regeneration is required.

If you reinstall Jellyfin (or its database gets rebuilt) and point the plugin back at your existing cache folder, the plugin now relinks every cached entry to your library automatically — no re-encoding, no lost cache.

- New: orphaned cache entries (from a reinstall or database rebuild) are automatically relinked to your items at server startup and before every scheduled prune run.
- New: the dashboard shows a warning banner with a one-click "Relink orphaned entries" button whenever orphaned entries are detected.
- Fixed: Cache Status no longer counts orphaned entries as cached (previously it could show 100% coverage while every item listed as "not cached" and playback re-encoded).
- Fixed: the daily prune task no longer deletes a reinstalled server's still-valid cache — it relinks first and only removes entries that truly match nothing.

Update, restart your server once, and your cache reconnects on its own within about 30 seconds — or press the new Relink button on the plugin dashboard.

Fixes playback stalling on Apple TV when audio is passed through unchanged (stream copy). The playlist could advertise the wrong audio format, which made the player wait forever for audio it was never going to get. If playback ever froze right after turning subtitles off, this is that fix.
Fixed playback breaking on SDR variable-bitrate files when trickplay is enabled. Affected videos could freeze mid-playback or get stuck on a loading screen when resumed; they now play normally.

* On HDR sources, tone mapping now runs on the GPU when your ffmpeg build supports it (OpenCL for Intel QSV / VAAPI / AMD on Linux, CUDA for NVIDIA, Metal on macOS). The previous CPU tone-mapping path was the dominant cost on HDR content — moving it to the GPU is the bulk of the speedup. Falls back to the old CPU path automatically when no GPU tone-mapping filter is available.

* The ffmpeg filter chain now thins frames down to the trickplay rate (one every couple of seconds) before any per-frame work runs. Previously every decoded frame was transferred GPU → CPU before being discarded — for a 2-hour 4K HDR source that's hundreds of thousands of wasted full-resolution transfers.

* New "GPU tone-mapping for HDR" toggle in the plugin settings, on by default. Disable it if GPU tone-mapping misbehaves on your hardware — encodes still benefit from the filter-chain reorder.

* Encodes that hit a GPU tone-mapping issue now fall back to CPU tone-mapping automatically (keeping hardware decode), and only drop to full software decode if the hardware decoder itself fails. The dashboard's hardware-path column shows what's actually in use (e.g. "QSV+OCL", "VideoToolbox+VT") so you can see the path each encode is taking.

A user on an Intel iGPU reported that a 2-hour 4K HDR film took ~90 minutes to generate on the prior version. The same encode finishes in roughly 10 minutes on this version.

Previously, if you deleted a library from Jellyfin, the plugin's
"Find & select items" list and the daily pre-generation task kept
seeing items from the removed library until Jellyfin's next library
scan cleaned them up — which meant inflated totals on the dashboard
and the nightly task wasting time encoding files that were no longer
in any library.

The plugin now scopes its lookups to the libraries currently visible
in Jellyfin, so the moment you remove a library the dashboard total
matches the Cache Status widget and the pre-gen task stops touching
those items.

No action required — just update the plugin and the next dashboard
load will reflect the correct counts.

Avoids advertising an iframe trickplay variant whose playlist resolves
to a valid-but-empty stub on cache miss — that combination can stall
AVPlayer on tvOS 26 with seek-shifted on-demand transcodes. Trickplay
appears on the next playback session once the warmup task generates
the cache.

* Search results above 200 items now load progressively. Default page is 500; 'Load more' appends the next batch and 'Load all' pulls everything matching the current filter.
* New 'Select all N items matching this filter' link appears once you've checked some visible items in a paginated result. Click it to select every match — including items not yet rendered. The bulk Generate or Evict action then operates on the entire match set, not just the page in front of you.
* Selection persists across pagination — checking an item on page 1 stays checked when you load page 2.
* 'Clear selection' link in the banner dismisses an all-matching selection. Filter, sort, or search changes also reset selection automatically.

Cancel active encodings

* New "Cancel" button on each in-flight row in the Encoding-in-progress panel, plus a "Cancel all" button in the footer.
* Works for both queued items (waiting for an encoder slot) and items currently being encoded.
* Existing cached trickplay for the canceled item is preserved — only the in-progress attempt is dropped.
* Cancel is idempotent — a second click is harmless.

A user with a parental rating limit sees the Web UI sections narrowed to the titles that limit allows, rather than none of them. The home Discover row, the Want to watch row, and the item page rows each have a placement setting; existing settings carry over. The Gaps Report's toolbar is grouped by what each control acts on, every header has a select-all, a line above the list says how many rows the filters hide, and Add to TODO is now Add to watchlist. A new scheduled task, Prune gaps from deleted items, takes deleted library items out of the report: a gap they were the only source of is removed, and one with other sources moves to the next. It has no default schedule; it waits for a running scan, and a second scan waits for the first. Recommendation groups link to the owned title they came from. Books get an OpenLibrary id field and albums and artists a Discogs id field in the metadata editor, with a link on the item's page; a dedicated OpenLibrary or Discogs plugin takes over when installed. Links are built from each title's ids when the report loads, so a link plugin installed later applies everywhere. The report takes far less memory and disk (on a library with 83,000 gaps, about 1.6 GB down to 200 MB in memory and 245 MB down to 131 MB on disk), loads in about half the time, and is written far less often during scans and where-to-watch lookups. Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. With Everyone's watchlist on (off by default), that same household list is a Discover source and leads the Discover view of every domain it has entries for. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. The report's Send action has a quality profile picker, filled from the stack's own profile list and preselecting the profile you configured, so an older title the default profile cannot find a release for can still be sent. The report's My TODO list popup is gone; the Fulfillment queue is where an administrator sees every list. The report's multi-select bar can Acquire, Request, or Resolve a checked batch (Resolve applies one shared note), alongside Mint and Add to TODO. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. With "Want to watch: move arrived titles into a playlist" on, a title that is in the library moves into that user's own Jellyfin playlist the next time it is verified, so it shows up in every client. The playlist is named Want to Watch unless you change it, and only a real file counts as arrived. Amazon and web-search links for a book or album include the author or artist, on the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue. TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are set with the same chip pickers the other curated sources use. A book's dialog loads its description from OpenLibrary when you open it. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. A library that sets a metadata fetcher order keeps TVmaze in the series check. TVmaze is not a Jellyfin metadata fetcher, so it is always asked and ranked last.

The home page can show a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found from titles you own and from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), never from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, a trailer link, and a link to the title's JustWatch page, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. versions.changelog:
Recognition is far more accurate and roughly three times faster. The bundled Latin database carries glyph shapes trained on real disc fonts, so few characters read as the unknown box. A file gives up every subtitle track in one pass rather than one pass per track, tracks recognize in parallel (Max parallelism leaves half the cores to playback), and image buffers are reused, so a run no longer drives the full garbage collections that interrupt playback. The matcher takes the best matching glyph rather than the first the database lists, reads case from the image's own x-height and cap height, splits a merged glyph pair, matches a multi-segment glyph on shape at any size, and follows the line's italic state so a stray mid-word italic reads as the run around it. Whether a track is light text on a dark outline or the reverse is read off the track itself, per track, so the Invert luma setting is gone, and word spacing is calibrated to real disc fonts.
Output keeps more of the disc. ASS carries the color the subtitles were drawn in as its style, with an override only on the lines that differ, places an off-center sign on the full alignment grid, escapes a literal brace, and rounds its timecodes; Auto picks ASS for a track that is positioned or uses more than one color. A cue never ends after the next one begins, a too-short cue is held to a 750 ms readable minimum, and a re-sent duplicate cue merges with its neighbor.
Text correction covers misread digits (a 1 between letters as l or I, a 0 as o), the two-letter words It, Is, In and If, a lowercase l after a speaker label, split contractions and quotes, punctuation spacing, a leading speaker dash, curly quotes, and padded sound-cue brackets. An accented Latin letter foreign to the track's language folds to its base ("Nothing" for "Nothińg"), keeping each language's own accents and leaving cast and character names alone. Spell-check protects names in singular and plural and runs before sentence casing, so a misread at the start of a line resolves against the dictionary instead of freezing into a name. The l-to-I fixes are English-only, so French keeps its elided articles. Language and hearing-impaired detection read a cue's words, not its markup, so close languages like Danish and Norwegian separate, and a track the database cannot really read is discarded rather than shipped.
The extraction log is its own dashboard page, with a Reprocess all button that runs the reprocess task and shows its progress, and a per-row reprocess for a single item. New settings: Fold foreign accents (on), and Aggressive OCR fixes (off) for the riskier digit twins 5/S and 8/B on a poorly scanned disc. The plugin is built against 10.11.0, the target ABI it declares, so it loads on every 10.11 server.

Output format is now selectable: SRT, ASS, or Auto, which decides per track and writes ASS only when a cue sits away from the bottom of the screen (PGS carries the position), so an ordinary track keeps the universally supported format. OCR text is spell-checked with Hunspell, protecting Title-case proper nouns and words drawn from the item's Jellyfin metadata (title, overview, series, cast and character names) so show and character names survive. Subtitle Edit OCR fix replace lists are applied when present; dictionaries and fix lists download on demand and re-download once older than a configurable age. A track with an undetermined language now has one detected from its OCR text and is named accordingly, and the track title, forced, hearing-impaired, and commentary flags appear in the file name so commentary tracks are identifiable. A hearing-impaired track is recognized from its own text when the source flags nothing, which is the norm for a remuxed disc. New OCR corrections cover misread apostrophes in contractions, mid-word capital X, V, and I, optional ellipsis folding, and bogus italic runs around single characters and punctuation. An unread glyph now costs nothing when matching a word against the dictionary, so "batt□e" resolves to "battle" and a damaged name can be restored from the item's metadata. A new "Reprocess extracted subtitles" task re-OCRs every logged file from its source with the current settings. Each file is probed with a single ffprobe pass rather than two, and only one OCR or reprocess task runs at a time.

Detect image-based subtitles by probing every Movie and Episode with ffprobe, since Jellyfin does not store PGS/VobSub streams in its metadata. A per-file cache skips files that are unchanged and were probed within a configurable window, with a force-rescan option. Word spacing now scales with subtitle line height, fixing spaces inserted between every letter on HD Blu-ray text. New options: extract only selected languages, discard a track whose dropped-event ratio is too high (removing any stale SRT), and a filename tag ({name}.{lang}.OCR.srt, shown as the subtitle title) so the plugin only ever overwrites or deletes its own output. A config-page modal lists every extracted file with a link to its movie or episode. The scheduled task now sits under its own category.

Initial production release. OCRs embedded image-based subtitles (VobSub/DVD and PGS/Blu-ray) to SRT files using nOCR pattern matching, with Subtitle Edit-compatible .nocr databases. versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). v3.0.1.2 - Discovery background work respects its master switch, Trakt travels with backup

- Seerr discovery generation and the Trakt refresh no longer run while Discovery user access is off; stored choices resume automatically on re-enabling
- Backup export/import round-trips the "Enable Trakt discovery" flag, so the choice survives a move to a fresh installation
- The Trakt checkbox only appears with Discovery on and the official Trakt plugin detected, and auto-saves like the Discovery toggle
- DryRun warms discovery caches without persisting, and leaves the shared trending pool untouched
- Greyed-out settings are now truly inert (keyboard and screen readers), and unsaved-changes tracking no longer reports phantom edits
- Tested by 6800 unit tests and 369 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.1.1 - "Trakt for you" no longer stays empty; discovery is quieter and self-healing

- Fixed the main report: "Trakt for you" could stay empty while trending and the local picks were full. Virtual stub library entries (real-looking files with a TMDb id but no media, created by some request helpers) were counted as owned and silently excluded every personal pick. They are now recognised as virtual and ignored, so your Trakt recommendations come through
- An empty "Trakt for you" is no longer sticky: a null or empty result is cached only briefly, so once the server has your picks they appear on the next open instead of being held behind a stale empty view
- A rate-limited or unreachable Trakt is retried with a backoff (honouring the server's Retry-After) instead of being re-hit on every tab load, and the same account open on two devices now shares one fetch instead of firing two
- An unlinked user no longer sees a "Trakt for you" tab that only shows a not-linked message; the tab appears once you are linked, and "Trakt trending" (which needs no login) is always available
- The plugin log now explains an empty personal result in one line (what was fetched, what survived, and why), so a token, fetch, or ownership issue is far easier to pin down
- Tested by 6779 unit tests and 369 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6
- Special thanks to @TheColin21 (https://github.com/TheColin21) for finding and reporting the empty "Trakt for you" issue and for debugging it together ❤️

v3.0.1.0 - Trakt discovery + encrypted secrets, Discovery tab no longer goes blank on Jellyfin 12

- New Trakt discovery source: when the official Jellyfin Trakt plugin is installed, the Discovery tab gains two sub-tabs beside the local picks, "Trakt for you" (your personal Trakt recommendations) and "Trakt trending" (global, no login), using the same card layout, request/dismiss mechanics, and per-user ML scoring. The Helper has no Trakt app of its own: it sources everything read-only through the official plugin's connection, so there is nothing to configure per user and no second app to register. A single "Enable Trakt discovery" checkbox (shown only when the official plugin is detected) turns it on
- All stored credentials (Seerr and Arr API keys) are now encrypted at rest with Data Protection and never logged in plain text; backups stay portable and re-encrypt on restore
- The Seerr Discovery custom tab reliably shows its content again on Jellyfin 12: navigating away and back no longer leaves it blank
- Returning to the tab is instant and never flashes a spinner: the last results render immediately from memory, and newer suggestions are swapped in silently in the background when a scheduled run has produced them
- The sidebar "Seerr Discovery" link opens the tab correctly on the modern Jellyfin 12 layout (both the top header and the narrow-screen menu), as well as on the classic layout
- The Codecs tab cards can now be rearranged by dragging a card's header handle (long-press on touch, with edge auto-scroll) or by keyboard (Enter to grab, arrow keys to move, Enter to drop, Escape to cancel); the order saves instantly, survives refresh/restart/update, and travels with backup export/import
- Radarr/Sonarr instances behind a reverse proxy with a private CA, self-signed, or IP certificate can now connect via a per-instance "Skip certificate validation" checkbox in Settings
- Recommendations now follow completed franchises: a series you finished years ago is surfaced again when a new entry arrives, instead of being outranked by whatever you watched most recently
- Recommendation explanations are now concrete: the "Why" line names what actually drove the pick (completing a collection, a franchise, a matched writer/country/era, or genuine crowd popularity) instead of a vague "Recommended for you". Discovery suggestions keep their person/genre/trending/popularity reasons, now with an honest fallback instead of claiming "Popular and highly rated" for a title that is neither
- Hardening: API keys, the log filter, and backup credentials now reject hidden control characters that could cause errors or log tampering; odd-charset responses are read safely; and restoring a backup that disables TLS validation now warns you first
- Recommendation playlists are always private: playlist sync now sets visibility explicitly instead of relying on the server default, so each user's recommendations stay visible to that user only
- Tested by 6720 unit tests (expanded security, hardening, and performance coverage) and 368 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6
- Special thanks to @TheColin21 (https://github.com/TheColin21) for testing and donation ❤️
- Special thanks to Daniel for his donation ❤️
- Special thanks to @baervers23 (https://github.com/baervers23) for great input and ideas ❤️

v3.0.0.4 - Per-library file counts, boxset link fix

- The Per-Library Breakdown now shows a file count below every size value (trickplay folders included), so sparse and dense libraries are distinguishable at a glance
- Boxset library rows no longer link into the Library Explorer, whose scope excludes boxsets; they render as plain text instead of opening an empty state
- Every task dropdown in Settings now explains what the task does, via an info button next to each task name, in all dashboard languages
- The Overview Trickplay card now also shows the space used by trickplay images Jellyfin stores internally, on its own line below the alongside-media total, marked with an (internal) badge, or as the headline when no alongside data exists
- Compact log view on phones: log entries stack as cards below 700 px instead of squeezing into a four-column table, so no horizontal scrolling is needed, and rows keep breathing room at the screen edges
- Roomier Library Explorer filter popovers on phones using nearly the full viewport width, like the bitrate editor
- Tested by 6219 unit tests and 352 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.3 - Library Explorer, new Codecs breakdowns, disabled users ignored

- The Codecs tab now has a Library Explorer: combine resolution, codecs, bitrate, languages, watched users and formats into one search, scoped to the libraries you pick in its multi-select, so you can find e.g. all 4K films with low bitrate
- Options with zero matches under the other filters are hidden automatically, dimensions without matches stay greyed out, and multi-value dropdowns accept several audio languages, subtitle languages or users at once
- Every active filter is shown in the result header and a Reset button clears the whole search; results arrive as the familiar grouped file tree with Movies, TV Shows and other sections
- Jump straight into the search from the Overview: each library name and all four media cards open the Explorer pre-filtered to that scope
- Every categorical filter can be negated with Includes/Excludes, so you can search e.g. audio languages that are not German; excluded picks show as ≠ pills and counts preview what stays
- Four new breakdowns in the Codecs tab, each with drill-down to the exact files: Video Bitrate (7 tiers from < 2 to > 60 Mbps), Audio Languages, Subtitle Languages and Watched (by username plus Never watched)
- Each bitrate tier uses what Jellyfin measured for the video stream; when a file has no per-stream value the average is estimated from its size and runtime, so almost every file lands in a real tier instead of Unknown
- Disabled Jellyfin users no longer skew results: their old plays are excluded from Smart Recommendations, watch history and the new Watched breakdown
- Long breakdowns start collapsed behind a Show-all toggle with Unknown always last, and unreadable language tags fold into Unknown instead of junk entries
- Added responsive, independently scrollable library result cards.
- Improved compact layouts for mobile controls.
- Added consistent themed scrollbar styling across plugin panels and lists.
- The Overview Per-Library Breakdown has a new Other column per library covering NFO files, text files and other unrecognized sidecar files, plus a Books column whenever a book library exists, so every row adds up exactly to its Total
- Tested by 6169 unit tests and 341 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.2 - Log tab, save bar, resolution and touch fixes

- Clearing the plugin log no longer briefly shows a false "Failed to clear logs." error: the Clear button now confirms success immediately and refreshes the view right away
- Genuine clear failures (e.g. expired session or server error) now write a structured diagnostic to the browser console with the HTTP status and error kind, alongside the visible red button feedback, so a real problem is never silent
- Save bar no longer crowds on phones: the unsaved-changes label and Save button now stack on narrow screens, so long translations like the German "Nicht gespeichert" are no longer cut off
- Widescreen films are counted at their real resolution: cinemascope masters like 1920x800 or 1920x1040 are now correctly shown as 1080p instead of 720p in the Codecs tab, decided by whichever axis reaches a resolution class
- The resolution drill-down now lists each file's exact pixel dimensions (e.g. 1920x800) next to its name, readable on desktop and phones
- Chart tooltips work reliably on touch: the first tap on the Trends chart or a Codecs ring now shows and keeps the tooltip instead of flashing it away, and a second tap on the same Codecs segment closes it
- The save confirmation only appears after a real save: reverting a setting back to its original value no longer briefly shows "All changes saved"
- Tested by 5535 unit tests and 320 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.1 - Per-instance library allocation for Arr

- Assign specific Jellyfin libraries to each Radarr/Sonarr instance, so the Arr tab compares an instance only against the libraries it manages
- With two or more instances of a type, each gets a picker in Settings listing only the matching kind of library (movies for Radarr, TV for Sonarr)
- Leave a picker empty to keep it automatic: instances are matched to libraries from their root folders
- Assignments are kept across backup and restore
- Fixes a 4K instance flagging every 1080p film as "not in Radarr"
- Tested by 5499 unit tests and 318 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.0 - Major release for Jellyfin 12.0+

- Books in your library overview: eBook libraries now show their size and file count on the Overview tab and count towards your storage totals, and they're always protected from every cleanup task
- Smarter recommendations: a much bigger model, fairer suggestions for brand-new users, and more variety in your top picks (no more ten near-identical films in a row)
- Recommendations now also learn from franchises/collections, country of origin, collection & folder themes, whether a series is finished or ongoing, writers/creators, top-billed cast, and how rare a genre or studio is in your library (each signal is optional per item, so missing metadata never skews a pick)
- Fresh picks appear between nightly runs, and faster generation on big libraries
- Redesigned Settings, Health and Arr tabs with a live 'reachable' indicator, plus a sticky save bar and unsaved-changes warning
- Better on phones
- Stronger security: API keys are never shown to the browser, backups can leave keys out, and cleanup can never delete or touch anything outside your media libraries
- Safer trash and cleanup: turning retention off really turns it off, trashing a shortcut never removes the file it points to, and Windows shortcut handling is fixed
- More accurate library stats and safer Seerr request cleanup
- More reliable saves and backups (no more rare 'lost save' when antivirus is scanning)
- New end-to-end test suite runs the plugin inside a real Jellyfin 12 server on every change and proves cleanup stays inside your libraries
- Note: your recommendation model retrains from scratch after upgrading, so suggestions settle back in over the next scheduled runs
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

versions.changelog: v2.4.2 'Genre and studio badges that count what you watched' - FIXED (#154, thanks @mattsigal for his first PR, with once-per-item counting by @camarigor): TV episodes now credit studio badges with their series' studios (It's Not TV, Auntie Beeb and Netflix and Watch only ever saw movies); TMDb composite genres count for each part ('Action & Adventure' for Action Hero, 'Sci-Fi & Fantasy' for Sci-Fi Scholar and Fantasy Forever) and 'Sci-Fi' counts as 'Science Fiction'; studios match as a whole word plus aliases ('Walt Disney Pictures' counts for Disney, 'HBO Max' for HBO); every item counts once per badge however many of its names match. WHEN YOU UPDATE: watches already in your history start counting, so progress jumps and badges can unlock on the spot (on our server: 11 genre badges across 23 profiles, no progress went down); custom genre and studio badges match the same way (a custom 'War' badge now counts 'War & Politics'); episode plays from before this update stored no studio, so TV credit on studio badges starts now. Both assemblies were stamped x.y.z.0, so the dashboard showed 2.4.0.0 for an install the manifest called 2.4.0.1 - the plugin image 404'd and UNINSTALL FAILED OUTRIGHT. Each package now stamps the version it ships as. Stuck on 2.4.0.1? Updating through the catalogue is enough; the restart that loads the new build removes the old folder. FIXED (#141, @Roboatlas21): the page worked in a private window and nowhere else. A browser that cached Jellyfin's page before the plugin was installed revalidates it, Jellyfin answers 304 from the file on disk, and a 304 has no body to inject into - so the browser kept using a copy with no plugin in it. Worst where the web directory is read-only, since the on-disk patch cannot take either. The middleware now forces a full page while the patch has not taken. No need to clear browsing data; a normal reload is enough. CHANGED (#129, @Tschiyo): the targeted badge cap is a setting, 1 to 1000, default still 50, with the targets past it named on the page; the per-play check no longer grows with the target count (ancestor-set lookup, cached collection/playlist members). FIXED (#133, @clarjon1): the Revamp style reached the rest of Jellyfin - invisible checkboxes, text inputs losing border and height, selection colour changing everywhere, on Jellyfin's own controls and every other plugin's settings page. Twelve rules are now anchored to this plugin's own surfaces. FIXED (#131, @Borededdy): a Custom Tab rendered nothing under a theme that ships its own copy of Jellyfin's home page (Abyss); the plugin now builds the missing panel itself. NEW (#136, @Verdancy-Rin): a top-center toast placement plus an admin default for users who have not picked one; also fixed - the default UI style (#43) was never stored, and every main config save switched the page integrations back off. FIXED: this plugin had been returning 500 for the whole server's /api-docs/openapi.json since 2.1.0 - its MediaType enum collided with Jellyfin's own type name and took the entire OpenAPI document down, breaking Swagger UI and every spec-driven client, silently. # v2.6.4

A larger follow-up to v2.6.3 built almost entirely from contributor PRs: app passwords get safer and work for SSO and passkey accounts, admins can be alerted by email or Telegram, the setup page fits SSO-only users, and the dependency pins that held since the spring are finally lifted after live re-verification. Drop-in from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no config or data migration.

## App passwords

- **An app password no longer signs in to the Jellyfin web interface** *(#249, by @camarigor; #244).* App passwords are for native apps; accepting one in a browser session defeats the point. A native client (Symfonium, Findroid, Seerr, and the like) still uses them exactly as before.
- **SSO and passkey accounts can create app passwords** *(#252/#248, by @camarigor).* Accounts that sign in through an identity provider or with a passkey, and so have no TOTP, were stuck with no way to make an app password for a native client. A linked provider (or a passkey) now satisfies the step-up that creating one requires.

## Sign-in and setup

- **Hide the plugin's 2FA setup from SSO users** *(#250/#247, by @camarigor).* An opt-in admin setting: a non-admin who signs in through a linked provider sees that the provider handles sign-in instead of the plugin's own TOTP/passkey enrolment. Administrators keep the full page.
- **A clearer authenticator rotation flow** *(#255/#254, by @camarigor).* The setup page shows the rotate card, and your old authenticator keeps working until the new one is confirmed.
- **OIDC errors tell a refused sign-in apart from an expired code** *(#234/#64, by @camarigor).*
- **The login page works behind an access proxy** *(#253/#251, by @camarigor):* the plugin's own requests now carry the page's cookies.
- **The admin Users tab saves an edited email reliably** through the step-up prompt *(#264/#263, by @camarigor).*

## Notifications and detection

- **Admin alert emails, and Telegram as a channel** *(#261/#259, by @camarigor).* Security events (suspicious sign-in, emergency lockout) can now notify admins by email or Telegram.
- **Turn suspicious-login detection off** *(#260/#258, by @camarigor),* and leave impossible-travel out of the security score when geo checks run elsewhere.

## Correctness

- **Sign-in no longer saves a stale copy of the user record** *(#257/#256, by @camarigor),* which could drop a concurrent change made during sign-in.

## Dependencies

- **The QuestPDF and IdentityModel pins are lifted** *(#262, by @camarigor).* `Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens` / `System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt` move to 8.23.0 and QuestPDF to 2026.9.1, after re-verifying a live OIDC sign-in and the recovery-code PDF on both the 10.11 and 12 builds. The spring OIDC regression turned out to be a missing bundled assembly, shipped since v2.6.2, not the library. Fido2 moves to 4.2.0 and MailKit to 4.18.1. The Jellyfin runtime references stay pinned.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no schema or configuration migration. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published and your server selects the right one automatically. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested.

# v2.6.3

A safety release on top of v2.6.2: uninstalling, disabling, or losing the plugin no longer locks out the accounts that used it. Drop-in from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no config or data migration.

## Accounts are handed back to Jellyfin when the plugin goes away

*(Fixes #232, seen in #213, by @camarigor.)*

Signing in with a passkey, creating an app password, or using the OIDC bridge moves an account onto the plugin's own sign-in provider, and nothing moved it back. So once the plugin was uninstalled, disabled, or failed to load, Jellyfin refused every sign-in for those accounts, administrators included.

The plugin now hands those accounts back to Jellyfin's own authentication provider when it is uninstalled or disabled, and takes them back the next time it starts (so an app password created before the uninstall works again after a reinstall). Concretely:

- **Uninstall** moves every account on the plugin's provider back to the provider the plugin was delegating password checks to (Jellyfin's default on a stock server), before Jellyfin removes the plugin.
- **Disable** does the same, through a filter that runs after Jellyfin disables the plugin.
- **Reinstall / re-enable** then restores those accounts to the plugin on the next start, each only while it is still on the handed-back provider.

The hand-back only ever runs on an administrator's own uninstall or disable, and only moves accounts that are actually on the plugin's provider; while the plugin is running, nothing changes.

## Recovery when the plugin cannot load

No code can run for a plugin folder that was deleted or a build that will not load, so the README now documents the ways out: re-enable and restart, save the account's profile page (which moves it to the default provider), or the two-line `sqlite3` fix with Jellyfin stopped.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no schema or configuration migration. The only new on-disk state is a short-lived `handed-back.json` that exists between a hand-back and the next start. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published and your server selects the right one automatically. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested.

# v2.6.1

A focused fix release on top of v2.6.0: OIDC sign-in now hands off to the 2FA prompt correctly when a user has both SSO and plugin TOTP, and a native-library crash that could core-dump the whole Jellyfin process is gone. Drop-in from any 2.5.x or 2.6.0, with no config or data migration.

## OIDC sign-in reaches the 2FA prompt instead of erroring

*(Fixes #204, by @Faffu.)*

If a user signed in with OIDC/SSO **and** also had plugin TOTP enabled, the sign-in stopped on the callback page with **"Sign-in could not be completed. Error: HTTP 401"**. That 401 was actually the expected `TwoFactorRequired` response with a challenge token, but the bridge page treated any 401 as a terminal failure and never opened the TOTP page.

Both sign-in bridges (the browser callback and the in-app webview) now recognise a `TwoFactorRequired` response and continue to the existing 2FA challenge, then complete sign-in once the code is accepted. A wrong code is still rejected, an ordinary 401 is still an authentication failure, and credentials are not stored before the second factor is completed. The challenge redirect is built from the server's own base path, never from anything in the response.

## No more `libsodium` core dumps

*(Fixes #203, reported by @bluej007.)*

On some hosts (seen on the linuxserver.io image on Jellyfin 12) the Jellyfin process could randomly core-dump while browsing the dashboard, with the crash inside the dynamic linker loading `libsodium.so`.

The cause was the recovery-code PDF service eagerly loading `libsodium.so` as if it were a QuestPDF dependency. It is not: `libsodium` belongs to the passkey code (NSec), and loading it late from the PDF path meant even servers that never use passkeys pulled it in, where a late load of that library can crash glibc's loader outright. The PDF service now loads only its real native dependencies; `libsodium` is loaded on demand only when a passkey is actually used, so passkeys are unaffected and everyone else stops crashing.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x or 2.6.0, with no schema or configuration migration. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published for this version and your server selects the right one automatically. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested.

# v2.6.0

**Jellyfin 12 is supported.** This release ships a second build so the plugin loads and runs on Jellyfin 12 (which moved to .NET 10), while the existing build keeps serving Jellyfin 10.11.x exactly as before. Both live in the one plugin catalog under the same entry, so your server downloads the build that matches its version: there is nothing to pick and existing installs update themselves. It also fixes the admin step-up prompt on the settings save path and the OIDC provider form, and makes the GeoIP diagnostics finally explain themselves. Drop-in from any 2.5.x, with no config or data migration.

## Jellyfin 12 support, without dropping 10.11

*(Closes #196 and #172.)*

Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10, and a plugin compiled against 10.11 (.NET 9) will not load on it, which is why every action returned **401 / "Unauthorized"** on 12 (#172). Rather than fork the plugin or abandon 10.11 users, this release builds the **same source twice**:

- a **.NET 9** build for Jellyfin **10.11.x** hosts, and
- a **.NET 10** build for Jellyfin **12.x** hosts.

Both are published in the one `manifest.json` under the same plugin, keyed by the Jellyfin version each needs. Jellyfin's own catalog keeps the builds whose target version is at or below your server's and installs the newest, so a 12 server pulls the .NET 10 build, a 10.11 server pulls the .NET 9 build, and neither ever sees the other. **You do not choose a download**: the catalog and auto-update do it for you. If you install manually from the Releases page instead, grab the `-jf12` zip on Jellyfin 12 and the plain zip on 10.11.

Everything was verified end to end on a real Jellyfin 12 server and a Jellyfin 10.11 server: sign-in, refresh persistence, OIDC/SSO, TOTP, email OTP, recovery codes, passkeys, app passwords, admin step-up, the PDF recovery-code export, and the admin dashboard page.

**Related 12 fixes rolled in:**

- **#191** *(camarigor)*: in-app OIDC sign-in on 12 froze on a blank screen. On 12 the router asks for the server connection before the reconnect that 10.11 did first, so the stored credential (which had no resolvable address) left the client pointing at nothing. The sign-in bridge now stores the address it just authenticated against, in the connection mode 12 expects.
- **#193** *(camarigor)*: 12 changed some web routes, so the plugin's setup link and the way it re-enters the setup page needed updating. 12 users get a working way back to the setup page from the avatar menu.
- Completes the header work from v2.5.22 (#174/#180): the plugin's pages and endpoints accept Jellyfin's current `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token` header, which 12 requires once legacy authorization is disabled.

## The admin step-up prompt now appears everywhere it should

*(Closes #198 and #194; helps #189 and #148.)*

The server has gated the sensitive admin actions (creating, editing and deleting OIDC providers, toggling a user's 2FA, "require password setup", and reading the audit log) behind a **step-up** re-authentication since v2.5.6. But some of the admin page's own calls sent those requests with a plain `fetch`, so the server's `403 { stepUpRequired: true }` came back as a bare **"Save failed"** and, for provider **Delete**, nothing happened at all (#198). Adding an identity provider on a step-up-protected server was simply impossible.

- **#198 / #199** *(camarigor)*: the provider form and the shared admin helpers now go through the step-up-aware fetch that Save Settings has used since v2.5.8. When step-up is required you get the prompt; when something else fails you get the server's actual reason instead of a generic message.
- **#194 / #195** *(camarigor)*: the admin step-up modal previously accepted only a typed TOTP code, locking out admins whose second factor is an **emailed code** or a **passkey**. It now offers the emailed code and a passkey alongside TOTP, using the same unified proof the rest of the plugin uses.

If you hit "valid code rejected at step-up" on 10.11 (#189), please retest on this build: the step-up verification and the admin-call routing both changed here.

## GeoIP diagnostics that explain themselves

*(#200, camarigor. Refs #51.)*

Three people reported `GeoIP databases loaded = Fail` with the files in place, and none had a log line to go on, because the loader had nothing to say: it fixed the configured path before trying to open it, a file the process could not see was skipped in silence, and a failed load was never retried until the path changed or Jellyfin restarted. Now the loader keeps the reason, retries, and falls back to an in-memory open, and the Diagnostics tab prints what it saw for **each** database. A bad path no longer reads as a blank "Fail": it says, for example, `not found at /config/geoip/GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb (its directory is not visible to the Jellyfin process; checked as user root)` or `rejected (not absolute)`, so you can actually fix it.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x, with no schema or configuration migration. 500 tests pass. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published for this version; your server selects the right one automatically.

- ApplySonarrHasFile rewritten O(N*M) -> O(N). HashSet + List.RemoveAll instead of repeated List.Remove; seasons indexed once.
- ignoredTvdb HashSet hoisted out of per-series loop.
